summary: Redwood AE+SE walked MediScan through the Model Catalog in the Console, focused on selecting open models, how we surface benchmark results and the compatibility matrix for deployment. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for inference of clinical note generation; concerns around latency tail, cost, and on-prem/private deployment for PHI. Agreed next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, security docs, and schedule a POC scoping call.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-12 15:30 PDT | Duration: ~46m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Ava (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Lina Park, Marcus Bell, Sofia Ruiz, Ethan Cho

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have a 45 minute block here, will run through the model catalog, show a couple of open models, benchmarks and compatibility matrix and then leave time for Q&A.
00:12 Dr. Lina Park: Thanks, Samir. Quick context - we're exploring options for generating clinical visit summaries from our ambulatory EHR notes, throughput is moderate but we care a lot about P95 latency and PHI separation.
00:25 Samir: Totally, that's the right lens. Ava will jump into the console demo and show how the catalog surfaces latency/cost tradeoffs and the matrix for CPU/GPU/quantized runs.
00:35 Ava: Alright opening the Console - so on the model catalog page you'll see curated open models and our Redwood-verified performance badges. Here we have models like Llama-2-13b, Vicuna variants, and a couple of optimized quantized builds. The catalog shows per-model stats: tokens/sec, P50/P95 with a sample batch size, and a cost-per-1k tokens estimate.
01:02 Marcus: When you say P95, is that measured on hosted infra or the dedicated racks?
01:08 Ava: Good question, the badge indicates the benchmark mode - we run a standard suite on hosted infra with the same hardware family as Dedicated; for Dedicated we run a separate profile. The console lets you switch the 'profile' to see Dedicated numbers or a private deployment estimate. Note: numbers have small variance based on sequence length and batch shape.
01:28 Sofia: And compatibility matrix? how do we know a model will run on our on-prem GPUs?
01:33 Ava: Right, go to the compatibility view - we map model architectures to recommended runtimes, supported quantization formats (int8, awq, q4f16), and kernel availability by GPU (A10, A100, 4090). There's also a column for 'KV cache friendly' vs models that require special attention.
01:50 Ethan: Quick, are your quantized builds open or do we need to do custom quantization for our data?
01:55 Ava: We provide pre-quantized variants for common families; you can also bring your own quantized artifact. For private deployments we support a pipeline for customer-side quantization with our toolset. There may be slight quality diff - we publish a delta in the benchmark spreadsheet.
02:15 Dr. Lina Park: This benchmark spreadsheet - is it actionable? Like can we replicate locally?
02:19 Samir: Yes, we attach a runbook and the harness; we'll share the link in the follow-up. It contains test harness config, sequence length distributions, and the raw logs for P50/P95 and throughput.
02:35 Marcus: Our main worry is tail latency - we get spikes around 300 tokens per request and P95 is what breaks SLAs. Can Redwood route to a lower-latency model or fall back?
02:45 Ava: You can configure smart routing policies - route to a lower-parameter variant or a quantized build when latency SLOs tighten. We also have automatic fallback to a cheaper model when Dedicated capacity is saturated.
03:02 Sofia: Security: we need KMS integration and audit logs, also SOC 2 and support for private control plane.
03:10 Samir: Absolutely - we support KMS/HSM integrations, per-request encryption at rest, SAML/SSO, and detailed audit logs; we'll attach the SOC2 and private deployment checklist.
03:20 Dr. Lina Park: How do you compare cost to OpenAI or Anthropic? our finance team keeps asking.
03:25 Samir: We published a unit economics comparison in the benchmark doc - cost per 1k tokens varies by batch size and quantization. For heavy throughput, our Dedicated reserved capacity often beats hosted third-party in unit cost, plus you get consistent tail latency. We should send a tailored example to you.
03:40 Jordan: I'll flag that we have an Optimize feature that recommends batching, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles per workload - it can run offline against a traffic sample.
03:52 Ethan: Is the Optimize recommendations automatic or do you need a POC?
03:55 Jordan: You can run a free analysis with a short traffic sample, we return a config and an expected cost/latency delta. For enterprise we do deeper profiling as part of a POC.
04:12 Ava: Back to the catalog - clicking into a model shows usage examples, safety notes, and the compatibility matrix; here we have a compatibility note that says 'Llama-2-13b-quantized-awq: supported on A100, 4090, but fallback to CPU is not recommended' (note: transcribed as 'a 100 four O nine O' in some exports).
04:37 Marcus: Are any of these models Redwood-maintained forks or are they straight upstream?
04:42 Ava: Mostly upstream open family models; we publish optimized variants and patches to improve inference friendliness (KV cache alignment, fused kernels). We label custom variants in the UI.
05:01 Dr. Lina Park: Any red flags for PHI? like do you store prompts or outputs on hosted?
05:08 Samir: Hosted API provides configurable retention policies; for PHI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with encryption and customer KMS. We'll share an architecture diagram.
05:22 Sofia Ruiz: One more on quantization quality - do you measure ROUGE or clinical-specific metrics?
05:28 Ava: We include both generic NLG metrics and can integrate your eval prompts to compute clinical metrics; Optimize ties regressions to your eval set and can alert on drift.
05:45 Dr. Lina Park: Great - what's the usual POC length to validate latency and quality?
05:48 Samir: Typical POCs are 3-6 weeks: first week for dataset exchange and baseline runs, two weeks for tuning and quantization, rest for validation and ops integration.
06:02 Marcus: Ok if we want to proceed how do we start - do we need an NDA?
06:06 Samir: We can start a non-sensitive pilot under a mutual NDA, or start with a data-minimized sample under our SaaS retention rules. We'll circulate the security packet.
06:20 Ethan: Could you show the console's benchmark visualization for a model variant?
06:24 Ava: Sure - switching to the 'benchmarks' tab... here you can toggle sample seq len 128/256/512, and compare P50/P95 side-by-side. See the shaded bands which represent variance.
06:40 Dr. Lina Park: I see the shaded band - what does it mean for real SLAs?
06:44 Ava: The band is 95% confidence from multiple runs; for SLAs we advise using P95 plus a small buffer, and consider caching common prefixes to reduce cost.
07:00 Marcus: Does the compatibility matrix export to CSV so we can share with infra?
07:03 Ava: Yes there's an export button, we'll send you the CSV and the annotated matrix.
07:10 Samir: To recap - we'll share: 1) model-compatibility matrix CSV, 2) benchmark spreadsheet + runbook, 3) SOC2 and private deployment checklist, 4) pricing examples for hosted vs dedicated. We'll also schedule a POC scoping call.
07:28 Dr. Lina Park: Sounds good, thanks.
07:33 Samir: Any final questions?
07:35 Sofia Ruiz: One last - do you have clients in healthcare doing PHI extraction?
07:38 Samir: Yes, we have several regulated customers; we'll anonymize references and share a case study where appropriate.
07:45 Marcus: Thanks everyone.
07:48 Meeting end: 16:16 PDT (approx)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., GPU names mangled, 'awq' transcribed as 'A W Q'), filler words and overlaps. Links referenced in meeting: model-compatibility matrix (link shared post-call), benchmark spreadsheet (link to shared drive), security packet (link to private docs).
